Dijon-Prenois · survey report

Circuit dijon · France · French GP (retired, classic:true) · theme green · day circuit (night:false) · base commit f0e2fca (branch cursor/dijon-survey-a1; the report ships in its tip commit) · surveyed 2026-10-15 · read-only: no js/ or css/ edits.
Both tooling merges applied: cursor/shared-shot-tooling-5b45 (weather shot tooling and gallery builder) and cursor/day-wet-lighting-b7b8 (PR #1979, day rain/storm no longer look like night). Captured with tools/shot/shot.mjs, TLX renderer, SwiftShader, 1280x720 frames.

1. Summary

  • Verdict: geometry builds cleanly (verify-track OK, 929 nodes, surface folds 0) and the circuit reads as open Burgundy hillside. The main open questions are where the landmark dressing sits against the real corners, plus weather and lighting responses that look engine-level.
  • 45 frames: 6 lap positions dry day orbit, wet/rain/overcast/fog/storm at day (3 positions each), dusk and night dry and rain (3 positions each), plus 12 eye-level frames.
  • Top findings are in section 7; evidence class is marked measured, source claim or guess.

6. Code & scenery deep-dive

  • Frame of reference. Everything is anchored with anchor(K(s), side, dist); dist is measured from the road edge (hw 7), so a gap of 11 puts the lap-wide armco 18 m from the centreline. +1 is the right side. With no start-line rotation (_sceneryShift none) the fractions in the file are the racing-lap fractions measured above.
  • Block vs corner check. Pouas (blocks 7-8, s 0.18-0.28) and Bretelle (block 13, s 0.61-0.69) agree with the measured right and left peaks. The inside tyre walls at Villeroy (:478-479, side +1) sit on the OUTSIDE of the measured left bend; the esses block (12) is on the inside of one sustained right.
  • Parabolique. Block 14 dresses s 0.684-0.796 (armco :545, tyre wall :546, bank :555, hoarding :547). The measured sustained right that closes the lap is s 0.805-0.887; block 16 there is apron, gravel, halls and a fence only (:592-608).
  • Spartan by design. Motorhome and transporter rows are omitted at three sites (:268-271, :592-595, :624-625) because awning posts buried 0.08-0.42 m; the audit baselines (ground buried 1, flatCoplanar 7) are the residue of that tuning.
  • Horizon. Seven ridgeAt slabs (:339, :340, :412, :413, :505, :509 and the 3 outcrops :755-757) and five far hills (:778-782) provide the skyline; the ridges are flat-topped boxes (see defect 6).
  • Lap-wide dressing (:629-757) is hash-driven: every(30) trees with a 50% skip, 17 near and 13 far hedge/fence runs, 20 crop fields, 8 vine parcels, 6 farmsteads, 6 sheds, 5 rapeseed fields, 3 poplar rows. All sit behind spotClear/runClear guards, so on this 3.8 km lap some are silently dropped (108 trees, 1 hill).
  • Lighting. night:false and lamp "none": no authored night dressing. js/lighting/atmosphere.js was changed by the lighting merge (+50 lines): the new day-wet grey deck runs for wet/rain/storm (:440-442) while the overcast and fog branches only flatten the horizon when raceTimeOfDay === "default" (:457 overcast, :491 fog).
  • Real-world cross-check. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijon-Prenois): GP layout 3.801 km, 12 turns, Parabolique added with the 1976 extension. docs/tracks/dijon.md cites RacingCircuits.info and the official history page; neither was re-fetched in this survey, so corner-by-corner handedness is not independently confirmed.

7. Ranked defects and suggested fixes (not applied)

  1. Parabolique dressing is ~300 m before the sustained right that closes the lap. measured Bank, armco, tyre wall and hoarding are anchored at s 0.684-0.796 (scenery/dijon.js:545-583, landmark dijon-parabolique-bank :555 at s 0.742) while the longest sustained right (R 110-143 m, s 0.805-0.887) has only generic dressing (:592-608). Suggest re-anchoring block 14 and the bank to s ≈ 0.80-0.87 on the outside (-1) after checking a real map; keep the model id so landmarks/dijon.json stays valid.
  2. Villeroy reads as left-handers, brief says "paired rights". measured vs source claim Peaks at s 0.418-0.439 are +k (left, R 52-75 m). Code treats +1 as inside: tyre walls :478-479, building :481, marshal :480. Either the OSM-derived line or the brief is wrong; if the line is right, move these to side -1 and rename the comments. Uncertain which is right.
  3. Overcast and fog show a blue sky at day. measured Frames 13-18 look like clear day with extra ground haze. Cause is engine-level: atmosphere.js:457 (overcast) and :491 (fog) flattens the horizon only when raceTimeOfDay === "default", and this capture used the explicit --tod day; the wet/rain/storm branches got _dayWetGreyDeck (:440-442) but overcast/fog did not. Not a Dijon-only issue.
  4. Wet/rain/storm render translucent lattice "ghost" trees. measured (frames 08, 09, 11, 12, 20, 21, 25-27, 31-33; also pale ghost trees at the edges of eye frames 42, 44) guess mechanism: instanced tree foliage drawn through a wet reflection or transparency pass. Not Dijon-specific; needs a renderer check on another track.
  5. Orbit at s=0 is occluded by the pit-garage mass and pit slab (frames 01, 07, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31): track and car are out of view. measured Cheap fix is a different camera for s=0 (eye frames 34, 40, 41 cover it); the garage box itself (:207, 13 x 92 m) is as briefed.
  6. Horizon ridges are flat-topped slabs with straight cut ends (frames 02, 03, 06, 39). measured Sources: ridgeAt :339-340 (300-340 m long, 17-20 m high), :412-413 (340-380 m, 18-21 m). Suggest shorter, lower, more tapering ridges, or move them behind the existing farHills.
  7. Lap-wide armco sits 11 m off the edge and is nearly invisible in orbit and eye frames. measured (:633) while docs say "guardrail close to the edge" (row 0.105; code :289 uses 9). Suggest gap 6-8 on straights if the real circuit is close-barriered. Low priority; real offsets not measured.
  8. Elevation is milder than the source claim. measured vs source claim Max built grade 6.7% vs the brief's 14% at the Parabolique; the 64-sample profile (circuit-elevations.js:14, one sample per ~58 m) smooths crests, and the brief calls blind crests the character. No fix without a better elevation source.
  9. Turns table clusters. measured dijon.js:48 lists 12 peaks that sit in five complexes; the left at s 0.313, the valley rights at 0.34-0.37 and the long right at 0.80-0.89 carry no turn marker. Affects turn labels and anything keyed by turn index.
  10. Unexplained warm light pools on the verge at night/dusk (frames 29, 30, 33, 43, 45) while the tarmac stays nearly black. guess engine lamp/headlight pools; the circuit has no lamps (furniture lamp "none"). Needs lightState to confirm.
  11. Audit baselines are the ceiling, not zero: clip 4 severe, coplanar 2, ground buried 1 / flatCoplanar 7; 108 trees and 1 far hill are guard-dropped. Fix only by editing the circuit; never loosen the baselines.
  12. Built length is 2.2% short of the real 3.801 km (3717 m). measured The brief says not to change the def; recorded for completeness.
  13. Tooling: the gallery builder mis-files storm frames and ignores --out DIR. measured WEATHER_TAIL (tools/track/build-gallery.cjs:41) lacks storm, so dijon-19..21-orbit-fNN-day-storm.png list as tod "unknown" with sector "orbit-fNN-day". The help text says --out DIR but only --out=DIR is read (:644), so the documented form silently writes into the tracked gallery/tracks. Gallery build of this branch (to a scratch dir): 45 Dijon frames from the branch, 143 shots over 30 circuits in total.

8. Not captured / uncertain

  • No trackside or aerial frames; only orbit and eye views. Dawn was not captured. Dusk and night cover dry and rain only; wet, overcast, fog and storm were captured at day only.
  • The weather x position matrix is trimmed: wet, rain, overcast, fog, storm have 3 positions (0, 0.33, 0.67) each, not 6; dusk and night 3 positions; eye rain/night 3 positions.
  • Overcast and fog used the explicit --tod day; the game's default time-of-day mode (where the horizon flatten applies) was not captured.
  • The orbit and eye cameras step round obstructions, so the framing of the same fraction can differ between weathers. Differences in prop positions between frames are not defects.
  • Real-world handedness of Villeroy, Pouas, the esses and the exact Parabolique location were not verified against the official circuit page or an aerial.
  • No physics, lap or driving checks were run; this is a static survey. Terrain-over-road and sunk-water checks rely on the frames only, with no ground-profile run.
  • The wet ghost-tree and night light-pool causes are guesses until tested on a second circuit with lightState.
